when: remote: Repository not found|Could not resolve to a Repository
say: That repository does not exist on the remote yet. Create it and push in one step: gh repo create NAME --private --source . --push

when: accepts 0 arg\(s\), received 1[\s\S]*auth switch|auth switch[\s\S]*accepts 0 arg
say: gh auth switch takes flags, not a name: gh auth switch --hostname github.com --user NAME. Check gh auth status first to see which accounts exist.
The push was refused because a secret was found in a commit. Do not force it through - remove the file from history or add it to .gitignore and commit again.
That flag or subcommand does not exist in this version. Run the command with --help and use what it actually lists instead of trying another guess.
grep is not a Windows command. You have a grep TOOL for searching file contents - use it. In sh, the equivalent is findstr.
That is a Unix command and this is cmd.exe. Windows equivalents: dir, type, del, move, where, findstr. Or run it through powershell.
findstr does not understand that pattern. It takes plain strings, not grep syntax: findstr "word" file. Use the grep tool for regular expressions.
cmd.exe does not treat ' as a quote, so the jq expression arrived broken. Use double quotes, or drop --jq and read the raw JSON.
Use git remote set-url origin URL to change it, instead of adding it again.
This directory is not a git repository. git init first, or cd to the right one.

when: Authentication failed for|could not read Username
say: Git has no usable credentials. Run gh auth status to see the accounts, gh auth switch --hostname github.com --user NAME to pick one, then gh auth setup-git so git uses it.

when: '\w[\w.-]*' is not recognized as an internal or external command
say: That program is not on PATH. Check with: where NAME. If you meant to run text or a sentence, that is not a shell command.

when: is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet
say: That is not a PowerShell cmdlet either. Verify the name with Get-Command before calling it again.

when: The system cannot find the path specified
say: The path does not exist. List the parent with dir /b before using it.
Denied by the OS. A file may be in use or the action needs an elevated shell - it will not succeed by retrying.
